chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Thalabah, from Abu al-Hasan Amr ibn Shaddad al-Azdi and al-Sari together, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man has the most right to his wealth as long as the soul is in him; if he bequeaths all of it, it is valid for him. Therefore, this report does not contradict the earlier reports which contain the ruling that the bequest is not executed for what exceeds one-third, for two reasons: one of them is that we carry this report upon the one who has no heir at all, neither close nor distant, nor a visible Imam; it was valid for him to bequeath all his wealth.
ai.seo_question: Can a person with no heirs bequeath their entire wealth or is it limited to one-third?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to resolve the apparent conflict between reports limiting bequests to one-third and those allowing full disposal, by distinguishing between cases with and without heirs. The scholar explains that the one-third restriction is primarily to protect the rights of inheritors, whereas a person with no heirs at all retains absolute authority over their entire estate. This interpretation aligns with the Shia principle that bequests are a right of the deceased but are constrained by the potential claims of the heirs.
